#crypto.subtle

The Web Cryptography API in windows and workers, in secure contexts: CryptoKey and all the operations of SubtleCrypto. The computations are on core:crypto, in the browser; the JavaScript engine never holds a key's material except while a key is being exported or cloned. It costs nothing until a script calls an operation (native/js/odin/web_crypto.js is evaluated then).

Checked: amazon.com (its scripts call importKey; without it the page stayed empty), and web-platform-tests WebCryptoAPI (wpt/expectations): of the subtests outside modern-algos and secure-curves, what fails is almost only P-521.

LayerFile
the descriptionapi/crypto.widl (generates wj.wr_CryptoKey_*, wj.wr_SubtleCrypto_* and the host table)
the browser sidesrc/page/bindings_crypto_subtle.odin (keys, DER, computations), src/page/bindings_crypto.odin (random values, digest)
the realm sidenative/js/odin/web_crypto.odin (CryptoKey, the natives) and web_crypto.js (conversions, normalization, usages, error names, JWK)
between realmsnative/js/odin/clone.odin (Crypto_Key)
the testsexamples/jsweb/webcrypto.js (jswebtest webcrypto), web-platform-tests WebCryptoAPI (wpt/expectations)

web_crypto.js, like web_wasm.js, is an exception to the rule of native/js/odin/prelude.odin (no JavaScript in the realm): it is not in the image, and its source is stripped.

#What there is

AlgorithmOperationsFormats
AES-GCM, AES-CBC, AES-CTRencrypt, decrypt, generateKey, wrapKey, unwrapKeyraw, jwk
AES-KWwrapKey, unwrapKey, generateKeyraw, jwk
HMACsign, verify, generateKeyraw, jwk
PBKDF2, HKDFderiveBits, deriveKeyraw (import only)
ECDSA (P-256, P-384)sign, verify, generateKeyraw (public), spki, pkcs8, jwk
ECDH (P-256, P-384)deriveBits, deriveKey, generateKeyraw (public), spki, pkcs8, jwk
RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, RSA-PSSsign, verify, generateKeyspki, pkcs8, jwk
RSA-OAEPencrypt, decrypt, wrapKey, unwrapKey, generateKeyspki, pkcs8, jwk
Ed25519sign, verify, generateKeyraw (public), spki, pkcs8, jwk
X25519deriveBits, deriveKey, generateKeyraw (public), spki, pkcs8, jwk

Hashes: SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512.

#The design

  1. The material stays in the browser. A Crypto_Key is an object of the page (CryptoKeyData); the realm holds a handle. It does not change once made and is counted, so a computation on another thread keeps it alive if the realm lets go of it.
  2. extractable is checked twice. web_crypto.js throws the specification's error; CryptoKey_export refuses what is secret in a key that is not extractable, whatever the realm asks. Usages are checked in the realm only.
  3. Off the page's thread. RSA, the curves, PBKDF2 and symmetric work on inputs of crypto.digest_offload_bytes or more run on the blocking pool; a worker has no pool and works on its own thread. The promise settles from a task either way.
  4. The library's ensures end the process, so bindings_crypto_subtle.odin checks sizes before it calls core:crypto, even what web_crypto.js has checked.
  5. What core:crypto does not do is here: CBC and AES-KW over its ECB; CTR's counter of length bits, in two runs of its 128-bit one; GCM tags shorter than 128 bits, by sealing twice (the keystream is the same both ways); DER, read and written by hand; compressed points, through core:crypto/_weierstrass.
  6. CryptoKey is native (generated from webcrypto.idl, wjr_CryptoKey_get_*): it holds a state made by web_crypto.js that a page never sees. What key.algorithm and key.usages return are copies: changing them changes nothing.
  7. Structured serialization (structuredClone, messages, IndexedDB, history) writes the key's description and CryptoKey_serialize's bytes, for a key that is not extractable too: a script does not see them, and a key must survive in IndexedDB. These bytes are the one way a non-extractable key's material enters the engine's memory, and what IndexedDB writes is not encrypted.

#What is not there

  • P-521: core:crypto has only P-256 and P-384. NotSupportedError.
  • RSA moduli over 4096 bits, public exponents over 32 bits (the library's limits): DataError. generateKey makes only the exponent 65537 (OperationError otherwise), of 1024 to 4096 bits. RSA keys of more than two primes: NotSupportedError. A private JWK needs all of p, q, dp, dq, qi.
  • The algorithms of modern-algos (Ed448, X448, SHA-3, ML-KEM, ML-DSA, AES-OCB, ChaCha20-Poly1305, Argon2, KMAC).
  • Stopping a computation: PBKDF2 with a huge iteration count holds a thread of the pool until it ends, and the browser's exit waits for it (host.blocking_destroy).
